items.content_html:
Description

removes the "firefox default-src: none svg sprite blocking issue" section from the default-src page.

Motivation

the section is about a firefox bug that got fixed in firefox 132 (bug 1773976). since then firefox applies img-src to svg <use href> loads like other browsers, so default-src 'none'; img-src 'self' just works and the workaround isn't needed anymore. the page already has a note saying it's fixed, which makes the section confusing to read.

Additional details

i checked it in a current firefox nightly with a small local server:

  • default-src 'none'; img-src 'self': sprite loads and renders
  • default-src 'self'; img-src 'none': sprite is blocked, so img-src is what controls it now
  • default-src 'none': blocked

the engineer who fixed the bug suggested mostly reverting #34592 (https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1773976#c15). the other two pages #34592 touched don't have the sprite text anymore, so this was the last bit. nothing else links to the removed anchor.

Related issues and pull requests

Fixes #36745
Relates to #34592
items.title: csp default-src: remove outdated firefox svg sprite section

items.content_html:
This updates CSSScale, its constructor, and its x, y, and z properties (CSS Typed OM API) to match the spec, and replaces the "To do" stub examples.

  • Fix the API link (it pointed to the CSSOM docs), and say it represents any scaling function, not just scale() and scale3d().
  • Remove text copied from CSSTranslate ("translating vector", and z moving the element towards the viewer), and say what the scale factors do.
  • Fix z, which said that setting it makes is2D false. z defaults to 1, and is2D decides whether it's used.
  • Add a Description covering numbers and CSSNumericValue values, percentages read from CSS, is2D, and toString().
  • Add examples to every page, including a live example that grows a box.

This covers the CSSScale items in the stub list at #28118 (comment)

Claude states this, but I have not verified it:

  • The example output was checked in Chromium, not Firefox.
  • The spec's x, y, and z setters only convert numbers, but Chromium (and the WPT tests) throw a TypeError for non-numbers. The docs don't mention setter checks.
  • The spec writes a 2D scale with equal x and y as scale(x), but Chromium writes scale(x, x). The examples avoid this case.

Related docs work can be tracked in #46594
items.title: CSSScale: fix pages and add examples

items.content_html:
This updates CSSTranslate, its constructor, and its x, y, and z properties (CSS Typed OM API) to match the spec, and replaces the "To do" stub examples.

  • Fix the API link (it pointed to the CSSOM docs), and say it represents any translation function, not just translate().
  • Add a Description covering the value types, is2D, and what toString() and toMatrix() return.
  • Give the type of the parameters and properties as a CSSNumericValue (they gave CSS types such as <length-percentage>).
  • Fix z, which said that having a z value makes the transform 3D. z defaults to 0px, and is2D decides whether it's used.
  • Add examples to every page, including a live example that moves a box.

This covers the CSSTranslate items in the stub list at #28118 (comment)

Claude states this, but I have not verified it:

  • The example output was checked in Chromium, not Firefox.
  • The spec doesn't define any checks when setting x, y, or z, but Chromium throws a TypeError for a value of the wrong type. The docs don't mention setter checks.

Related docs work can be tracked in #46594
items.title: CSSTranslate: fix pages and add examples

items.content_html:
Description

In the "Literal matching" example of the import maps section, the page is at https://example.com/welcome (no trailing slash), so ./shapes/square.js resolves to https://example.com/shapes/square.js, not https://example.com/welcome/shapes/square.js. This fixes that first URL; the following sentence about https://example.com/welcome/ already had the right one.

Motivation

The two sentences currently give the same URL for two different base URLs, which hides the point the paragraph is making about the trailing slash. The fixed URL also matches the one a few lines below ("The module at https://example.com/shapes/square.js will now be requested").

Additional details

new URL("./shapes/square.js", "https://example.com/welcome").href gives https://example.com/shapes/square.js.

Related issues and pull requests

Fixes #46630
items.title: Fix resolved URL in import map literal matching example

Description

Updates the three PlayCanvas pages under Games > 3D on the web for PlayCanvas engine 2.x and the current Editor, and replaces all Editor screenshots.

Motivation

The pages were written for a much older engine and Editor. The engine tutorial loads a non-module build, uses the legacy model component, and links to a download URL that serves an outdated build. The Editor tutorial describes a UI that no longer exists. Readers following either one today hit outdated or broken steps.

Additional details

  • Engine tutorial: loads PlayCanvas 2.24.2 as an ES module (import map or npm), switches to render components, handles canvas resizing, adds an optional WebGPU section, and fixes the live samples. Both samples were tested in Chrome with WebGL 2 and WebGPU.
  • Editor tutorial: steps rewritten for the current Editor. All screenshots were recaptured from a real run-through and compressed with filecheck --save-compression; the outdated login and project-page images are removed.
  • Overview pages: mention WebGL 2/WebGPU, the MIT license, CDN/npm usage, and the React and Web Components wrappers; links updated.

Disclosure: I work on PlayCanvas.

items.content_html:
Description

Removes the bare fangsong keyword from the font-family page (syntax block, values list, and the live example) and from the <generic-family> page (values list and the syntax line).

Motivation

No browser treats fangsong as a generic family keyword. It only does something on systems that happen to have a font named "FangSong" installed (Windows does), so the live example falls back to the default font everywhere else. The current spec doesn't have a bare fangsong keyword either. CSS Fonts 4 now uses generic(fangsong), which no browser supports yet, so I left that out too.

BCD already dropped fangsong, kai, khmer-mul and nastaliq from css.properties.font-family (mdn/browser-compat-data#29246), so these pages were the last place still listing it.

Additional details

  • None of the engines has it in their generic family keyword list: Chromium css_value_keywords.json5, WebKit CSSValueKeywords.in, and Gecko's GenericFontFamily enum in servo/components/style/values/computed/font.rs all stop at serif, sans-serif, cursive, fantasy, monospace, system-ui and math.
  • In Chrome 156, el.style.fontFamily = '"fangsong"' reads back as fangsong (no quotes), while "serif" and "math" keep their quotes. So Chrome parses it as an ordinary family name, not a keyword.
  • CSS Fonts 4 changes list: "Consistently use generic(fangsong) instead of fangsong, as the generic font family name."

Related issues and pull requests

Fixes #43412
items.title: Remove unsupported fangsong keyword from font-family and <generic-family>

items.content_html:
Description

Adds the bfcache blocking reasons that are in the HTML spec but missing from MDN, and makes the NotRestoredReasonDetails.reason page point to the full list.

Motivation

The reason page only showed three examples of user agent-specific reasons, so readers had no way to find values like sharedworker-message. The guide already has a full list, but it was missing five values the spec defines:

  • rtc-used-with-cache-control-no-store
  • sharedworker-message
  • sharedworker-with-no-active-client
  • websocket-used-with-cache-control-no-store
  • webtransport-used-with-cache-control-no-store

I added those to the guide, plus the spec's note under sharedworker saying browsers can report the two more specific shared worker reasons instead. I didn't copy the whole list onto the reason page. It links to the guide section instead, so there's one list to keep in sync.

Additional details

Spec list: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#nrr-details-struct

The shared worker values came from whatwg/html#12086.

I compared the reason strings in the spec source with the list in the guide, and they now match (52 values each). markdownlint-cli2, prettier -c and cspell pass on both files. I also built both pages with rari build and checked that the new links and the #user-agent_specific_blocking_reasons anchor resolve.

Related issues and pull requests

Fixes #42970
items.title: Add missing bfcache blocking reasons from the HTML spec

items.content_html:
Title: [Technical review] Add WebDriver Classic Delete Session and Status pages

Description

Added pages for the following commands of the Sessions chapter of WebDriver Classic:

  • Delete Session
  • Status

Spec links

  • https://w3c.github.io/webdriver/#delete-session
  • https://w3c.github.io/webdriver/#status

Compat quirks worth looking into:

Chrome

  • Delete Session with an unknown session ID. Deleting a session that had already been deleted, or one with an ID that never existed, returned 200 with {"value":null} in my test run, where the spec returns invalid session id. BCD shows Delete Session as supported since Chrome 65 with no note.
  • Outdated w3c note. BCD's Chrome entries for both commands say to include {"goog:chromeOptions": {"w3c": true}} in the capabilities. My test sessions didn't set it, and both commands returned W3C responses.

/cc @sadym-chromium for the BCD update.
items.title: [Technical review] Add WebDriver Classic Delete Session and Status pages

items.content_html:
Description

Clarify that the Content-Security-Policy: sandbox directive accepts zero or more space-separated tokens to lift specific restrictions, and provide an example demonstrating multiple values.

Motivation

The syntax section previously stated that <value> could optionally be "one of the following values", which could be interpreted as permitting only a single token at a time. In the CSP specification (both CSP Level 2 and Level 3), sandbox accepts space-separated tokens, similar to the iframe sandbox attribute. This change aligns the syntax description and adds an example with multiple values.

Additional details

  • W3C Content Security Policy Level 3 – Sandbox directive

Related issues and pull requests

Fixes #46609
items.title: docs(http): document multiple space-separated values for CSP sandbox directive

items.content_html: I'm auditing our JS docs against the ES spec to see which features are undocumented. I'm identifying some pretty glaring holes in our references. It's not that we don't need these pages; we already have places that would benefit from linking to them but have to link to guides or learning articles instead.
items.title: Document Array Initializer

items.content_html: 3 years ago I asked https://github.com/orgs/mdn/discussions/201. It never got a decisive conclusion. I decided it's not worth formally defining and MDN should be free to define optionality however the readers would perceive it. However, we should document the methods' length where its value is not derived from our notion of optionality, because that's actually an observable part of its behavior.
items.title: Add note about function length where param optionality differs
